questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with 6 hours of severe right lower quadrant pain. Her last menstrual period was about 6 weeks ago. Serum hCG is positive, and transvaginal ultrasound shows no gestational sac within the uterine cavity but reveals a mass in the right adnexa. The abnormally implanted pregnancy is most likely located in which of the following sites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interstitial segment of the uterine tube

explanation.summary: Tubal ectopic pregnancies most often implant in the ampulla, the normal site of fertilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla, the widest portion of the uterine tube. When the fertilized egg fails to progress into the uterine cavity, it implants where it already is, so most tubal ectopic pregnancies are ampullary.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Interstitial ectopics occur but are less common; they are notable for late, catastrophic rupture rather than frequency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The isthmus is a narrow segment adjacent to the uterus and is not the usual site of fertilization or implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped distal end bearing the fimbriae, not the typical implantation site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovarian implantation is possible in principle but the fertilized ovum typically lodges in the tube, at the ampullary site of fertilization.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman has a screening Papanicolaou smear showing a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion. She is referred for colposcopy with directed biopsy. Sampling of which of the following locations is most likely to identify the dysplastic focus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Internal os of the cervical canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Duct of the greater vestibular gland

explanation.summary: The squamocolumnar (transformation) zone is the most common site of cervical dysplasia and squamous cell carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The squamocolumnar junction lies where the stratified squamous ectocervix meets the simple columnar endocervix. This transformation zone is more than a histologic landmark: it is the most common location for cervical dysplasia and cervical squamous cell carcinoma to develop.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The internal os opens into the uterus at the far end of the cervical canal, away from the transformation zone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The vaginal fornix is lined by the same stratified squamous epithelium as the vagina but is not the characteristic site of cervical dysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The stratum basalis is the regenerative endometrial layer, unrelated to squamous dysplasia of the cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The greater vestibular gland lies at the posterior introitus and is associated with cysts and abscesses, not cervical dysplasia.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles completes menstruation, during which the superficial portion of her endometrium is shed. Which of the following structures is primarily responsible for regenerating the lost tissue?

explanation.summary: The stratum basalis is retained through the cycle and replenishes the shed stratum functionalis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endometrium has an upper functional layer that proliferates and sheds each cycle and a lower basal layer that is maintained throughout the menstrual cycle. The role of the stratum basalis is to replenish the functionalis tissue lost during menstruation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stratum functionalis is the layer that is shed; it cannot regenerate itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stratum vasculare is a smooth muscle layer of the myometrium responsible for contraction, not endometrial regeneration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The perimetrium is the serosal covering of the uterus and does not contribute to the endometrial lining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endocervical glands secrete mucus into the cervical canal and do not rebuild the endometrium.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 31-year-old primigravid woman at 39 weeks' gestation is in active labor with strong, regular uterine contractions. The layer of uterine wall generating most of this contractile force has which of the following histologic arrangements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Outer longitudinal pattern of smooth muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Middle crisscrossing pattern of smooth muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inner circular pattern of smooth muscle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Simple columnar epithelium with glands and stroma

explanation.summary: The stratum vasculare, the middle myometrial layer with a crisscrossing pattern, produces most uterine contraction during labor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The myometrium has three layers. The middle stratum vasculare has a crisscrossing fiber pattern and is responsible for most of the uterine contraction during labor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The longitudinal outer layer is the stratum supravasculare, which stabilizes the uterine wall rather than powering labor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The circular inner layer is the stratum subvasculare, which contracts during menses to help shed the functionalis and aids placental separation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Simple columnar epithelium with glands and stroma describes the endometrium, which is not contractile muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mesothelium over loose connective tissue describes the perimetrium (serosa), the outer covering of the uterus.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation develops dull left-sided pelvic discomfort attributed to venous congestion from compression of the vein draining her left ovary. Into which of the following does this vein normally empty?

explanation.summary: The left ovarian vein drains into the left renal vein, and its longer course makes it prone to compression.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right ovarian vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava, whereas the left ovarian vein drains into the left renal vein. The increased length of the left ovarian vein makes it more susceptible to compression, especially during pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Direct drainage into the inferior vena cava describes the right ovarian vein, not the left.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The internal iliac vein receives the uterine vein and other pelvic organ veins, not the ovarian vein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The external iliac vein drains the lower limb territory and joins the internal iliac to form the common iliac vein.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The common iliac vein is formed by the union of internal and external iliac veins; the ovarian vein does not empty into it.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman is diagnosed with a carcinoma confined to the left ovary. In planning staging surgery, the team samples the lymph nodes that receive the primary lymphatic drainage of the ovary. Which of the following nodal groups is the most appropriate first site to sample?

explanation.summary: Ovarian lymphatics follow the ovarian vessels and drain directly to the para-aortic nodes, bypassing pelvic nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most pelvic organs drain into the internal and external iliac lymph nodes, but the ovaries are the exception. Their lymphatic drainage follows their blood supply from the abdominal aorta, so they drain directly to the para-aortic lymph nodes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Internal iliac nodes receive drainage from most pelvic organs but not the primary drainage of the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.B: External iliac nodes likewise serve general pelvic drainage rather than the ovary's first echelon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Superficial inguinal nodes are not described as the drainage route of the ovaries.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Common iliac nodes lie downstream of the iliac groups and are not the ovary's direct drainage site.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman undergoes left oophorectomy. To control the ovarian vessels, the surgeon clamps and ligates the ligament attaching the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall. Which of the following structures is at greatest risk of injury during this step?

explanation.summary: The ureter passes inferior and posterior to the suspensory ligament of the ovary and is at risk during ligation of the ovarian vessels.
explanation.whyCorrect: The suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall and contains the ovarian vessels and lymphatics. Because the ureter passes inferior and posterior to this ligament, it can be injured when the ovarian vessels are ligated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The uterine artery relates to the ureter at the 'water under the bridge' crossing during hysterectomy, not within the suspensory ligament.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The round ligament runs from the uterine fundus through the inguinal canal to the labia majora, away from this ligation site.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The external iliac vein courses along the pelvic brim but is not the structure classically injured beneath the suspensory ligament.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pudendal nerve supplies the inferior vagina, external genitalia, and pelvic floor and is not encountered at this ligament.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman presents with a painful, fluctuant swelling at the posterior aspect of the vaginal introitus on the right side. The lesion most likely arises from a gland whose normal function is which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Secreting mucus to lubricate the vulva during arousal

choices.label: B
choices.text: Producing sebum for the hair-bearing labial skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Secreting mucus within the endocervical canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Releasing fluid at the paraurethral openings

choices.label: E
choices.text: Producing the fatty tissue of the mons pubis

explanation.summary: Bartholin (greater vestibular) glands at the posterior introitus secrete lubricating mucus and commonly form cysts or abscesses.
explanation.whyCorrect: The greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands are located at the posterior vaginal introitus and secrete mucus to lubricate the vulva, especially during sexual arousal. They are the glands most commonly associated with cysts or abscesses presenting as labial swellings.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sebaceous glands of the labia majora accompany hair follicles in the labial skin, not the posterior introitus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endocervical mucous glands lie in the cervical canal, far from the introitus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The paraurethral (Skene) glands open near the urethral meatus anteriorly, not at the posterior introitus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The mons pubis is a fatty tissue layer over the pubic symphysis, not a secretory gland.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A biopsy is taken from the wall of the mid-vagina of a healthy 35-year-old woman. Which of the following best describes the epithelium expected on histologic examination?

explanation.summary: The vagina is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium over a lamina propria and smooth muscle wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vaginal canal is an elastic muscular tube lined by non-keratinizing stratified squamous epithelium, with a lamina propria and a muscular layer of inner circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle beneath.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium covers the skin of the labia majora, not the vaginal canal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Simple columnar glandular epithelium lines the endocervix and uterine cavity, not the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines the uterine tubes, where the cilia beat toward the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Simple cuboidal mesothelium covers the surface of the ovary.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with a history of tubal scarring is found to have an ectopic pregnancy implanted in the interstitial portion of the uterine tube at the cornu. Compared with ectopic pregnancies elsewhere in the tube, which of the following best explains why this location carries a particularly high risk of severe hemorrhage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Surrounding myometrium permits prolonged growth before rupture

choices.label: B
choices.text: The interstitium is the widest and most distensible tubal segment

choices.label: C
choices.text: The interstitial lumen lacks any surrounding muscular support

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fertilization normally occurs within the interstitial segment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Beating cilia continually force the conceptus deeper into the wall

explanation.summary: Interstitial (cornual) ectopics are dangerous because the surrounding myometrium lets the pregnancy grow longer before rupture.
explanation.whyCorrect: The interstitium connects the isthmus to the uterine musculature at the cornua. Because the surrounding myometrium allows an interstitial ectopic pregnancy to grow longer before rupture, rupture occurs later and often results in severe hemorrhage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The ampulla, not the interstitium, is the widest portion of the tube; the interstitium is embedded in the uterine wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The opposite is true: the interstitium is surrounded by the muscular uterine wall, which is exactly why rupture is delayed and severe.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla, not the interstitial segment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tubal cilia beat toward the uterus to transport the ovum; they do not drive the conceptus into the uterine wall.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman who has had four vaginal deliveries reports pelvic pressure and a sensation of a vaginal bulge that worsens with standing. Examination shows descent of the uterus into the vaginal canal. Weakness of which of the following muscle groups, forming the deepest layer of pelvic floor support, most directly explains her condition?

choices.label: B
choices.text: External urethral sphincter and deep transverse perineal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superficial transverse perineal and external anal sphincter

explanation.summary: The pelvic diaphragm — levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus) plus coccygeus — is the deep layer whose failure underlies pelvic organ prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: The deepest of the three pelvic floor layers is the pelvic diaphragm, composed of the levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus) and coccygeus, and it provides the primary dynamic support of the uterus. When pelvic floor muscles and connective tissue no longer support the organs, prolapse such as uterine descent occurs; childbirth is a key risk factor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus belong to the superficial layer of the urogenital triangle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The external urethral sphincter and deep transverse perineal form the middle layer at the perineal membrane, not the pelvic diaphragm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obturator internus and piriformis are primarily hip muscles that act as the pelvic 'walls,' supporting organs only indirectly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The superficial transverse perineal and external anal sphincter are superficial-layer muscles, not the deep diaphragm.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: In a developing ovarian follicle, endocrine cells of the theca interna secrete progesterone and estrogen precursors. Which of the following cells is responsible for converting these precursors into estrogen?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stromal cells of the ovarian medulla

explanation.summary: Theca interna cells make estrogen precursors that granulosa cells convert to estrogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: The follicle's support cells are the granulosa cells (called follicle cells early on) and the thecal cells around the follicle. Endocrine cells of the theca interna secrete progesterone and estrogen precursors, and the granulosa cells convert those precursors to estrogen. Tumors can arise from both cell types (granulosa cell tumors and thecomas).

whyWrongByChoice.B: The oocyte is the germ cell within the follicle and does not perform this hormonal conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The simple cuboidal mesothelium merely covers the ovarian surface.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus albicans is the collagen-filled remnant left after the corpus luteum regresses; it is not steroidogenic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The ovarian medulla contains nerves, vessels, and lymphatics in stroma, not the estrogen-converting cells of the follicle.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: During a pelvic dissection, a first-year medical student identifies a ligament that extends from the lateral aspect of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine, separating the greater sciatic foramen from the lesser sciatic foramen. Which of the following ligaments has she identified?

explanation.summary: The sacrospinous ligament runs from the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine and, with the sacrotuberous ligament, converts the sciatic notches into foramina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The greater and lesser sciatic notches are converted into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina by the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments. The sacrospinous ligament specifically extends from the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine, so it lies between the two foramina; together the two ligaments stabilize the sacrum and define the boundaries of these foramina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The sacrotuberous ligament spans from the sacrum to the ischial tuberosity, not to the ischial spine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament anchors the cervix and upper vagina to the lateral pelvic wall; it is a visceral support, not a sacral-to-spine band.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The uterosacral ligament extends from the cervix to the sacrum to support the uterus posteriorly; it does not reach the ischial spine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The obturator membrane covers the obturator foramen anteriorly and has no role in forming the sciatic foramina.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman sustains a midline perineal laceration during vaginal delivery. The tear involves the central structure located at the junction of the urogenital triangle and the anal triangle. Which of the following structures is injured?

explanation.summary: The perineal body lies centrally at the junction of the urogenital and anal triangles of the perineum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The perineum, the region inferior to the pelvic diaphragm, is divided into the urogenital and anal triangles. The perineal body is located centrally at the junction of these two triangles, so a midline laceration extending between them injures this structure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The ischial tuberosities form the lateral boundaries of the perineum, not its central junction point.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The pubic symphysis bounds the perineum anteriorly and is bone-cartilage, not a central soft tissue structure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The coccyx bounds the perineum posteriorly and is not located at the junction of the two triangles.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The obturator membrane covers the obturator foramen in the pelvic wall and is not part of the perineum's midline.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A dermatopathologist examines a biopsy taken from one of the two smaller cutaneous folds immediately flanking the vaginal opening of a healthy 30-year-old woman. Which of the following histologic findings is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stratified squamous epithelium with hair follicles and sebaceous glands

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stratified squamous epithelium with abundant sebaceous glands but no hair follicles

choices.label: C
choices.text: Simple columnar epithelium with mucus-secreting tubular glands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ciliated columnar epithelium with a thin underlying lamina propria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Simple cuboidal mesothelium over dense connective tissue stroma

explanation.summary: The labia minora are lined by stratified squamous epithelium and contain abundant sebaceous glands but lack hair follicles.
explanation.whyCorrect: The labia minora are the two smaller folds located on each side of the vaginal opening. They are lined by stratified squamous epithelium and lack hair follicles, though they contain abundant sebaceous glands. This distinguishes them from the labia majora, which bear both hair and sebaceous glands.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skin with both hair follicles and sebaceous glands describes the labia majora, not the labia minora.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Simple columnar epithelium with mucus-secreting tubular glands describes the endocervix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines the uterine tubes, not the vulvar folds.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Simple cuboidal mesothelium covers the surface of the ovary, not the labia.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: During an anatomy small-group session, students examine the external genitalia of a female cadaver and identify the hood (prepuce) covering the glans of the clitoris. This hood is formed by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The anterior junction of the labia minora

choices.label: B
choices.text: The anterior junction of the labia majora

choices.label: C
choices.text: The inferior extension of the mons pubis

choices.label: D
choices.text: The posterior margin of the vestibule

choices.label: E
choices.text: The fusion of the two clitoral crura

explanation.summary: The clitoral hood (prepuce) is formed by the anterior junction of the labia minora.
explanation.whyCorrect: The clitoris consists of the glans, the body, and two crura, and it is covered by a hood (prepuce) formed by the anterior junction of the labia minora. Only the glans is external; the clitoris extends well beyond it beneath the vulvar tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The labia majora extend from the mons pubis to the perineum but do not fuse anteriorly to form the prepuce.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The mons pubis is a fatty tissue layer over the pubic symphysis; it does not form the clitoral hood.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The vestibule is the area enclosed by the labia minora containing the introitus and urethral meatus; its posterior margin is unrelated to the prepuce.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The crura are deep erectile components of the clitoris itself, not the covering fold over the glans.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman is noted on pelvic examination to have a small cystic swelling within the vestibule immediately adjacent to the external urethral meatus. The cyst most likely arises from which of the following glands?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sebaceous glands of the labia majora

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometrial glands of the stratum basalis

explanation.summary: The paraurethral (Skene's) glands lie in the vestibule near the external urethral meatus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vestibule is the area enclosed by the labia minora and contains the vaginal introitus, the external urethral meatus, and glands including the greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands and the paraurethral (Skene's) glands. A cystic lesion immediately adjacent to the urethral meatus localizes to the paraurethral glands.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands are located at the posterior vaginal introitus, not beside the urethral meatus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endocervical glands lie within the cervical canal, far from the vestibule.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sebaceous glands of the labia majora accompany the hair-bearing labial skin, not the periurethral vestibule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometrial glands are part of the uterine lining and do not occur in the vestibule.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A reproductive physiologist studies why sperm traverse the cervical canal readily at certain times but are impeded at other times in the same woman. Which of the following factors determines whether cervical mucus acts as a barrier to sperm or as a transport medium?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The direction of ciliary beating in the canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: The thickness of the ectocervical epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tone of cervical smooth muscle

explanation.summary: Cervical mucus can be a barrier to sperm or a transport medium depending on hormonal status.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cervix produces mucus that can either create a barrier to sperm or serve as a transport medium depending on the hormonal status of the person. The mucus is secreted by the simple columnar epithelium and tubular glands of the endocervix.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciliary beating toward the uterus is a feature of the uterine tube epithelium, not the determinant of cervical mucus behavior.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Effacement is the thinning of the cervix during parturition; it does not govern the sperm-permeability of mucus during the cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ectocervix is covered by stratified squamous epithelium that does not secrete mucus; its thickness does not set mucus properties.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The cervix contains only small amounts of smooth muscle, and muscle tone is not what switches mucus between barrier and transport roles.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 24-year-old primigravid woman in early labor undergoes serial cervical examinations showing progressive thinning and effacement of the cervix. Which of the following best describes the tissue composition of the structure undergoing this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mainly collagenous and elastic connective tissue with small amounts of smooth muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Predominantly smooth muscle arranged in three distinct contractile layers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Predominantly skeletal muscle under voluntary control of the canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glandular columnar epithelium overlying a thick layer of adipose tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: A single mesothelial layer resting on loose connective tissue

explanation.summary: The cervix is fibromuscular, composed mainly of collagenous and elastic connective tissue with only small amounts of smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cervix is composed mostly of fibromuscular tissue, mainly collagenous and elastic connective tissue with small amounts of smooth muscle present. During parturition it thins and effaces, allowing the fetus to pass through.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Three smooth muscle layers (supravasculare, vasculare, subvasculare) describe the myometrium of the uterine body, not the cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No part of the cervix is composed of voluntary skeletal muscle; voluntary pelvic floor muscles are separate structures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The endocervix has glandular columnar epithelium, but the cervical wall beneath is fibromuscular connective tissue, not adipose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mesothelium over loose connective tissue describes the perimetrium (serosa) of the uterus.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: During colposcopy of a 34-year-old woman, the physician visualizes the opening through which the cervical canal communicates with the vaginal canal. Which of the following structures is being visualized?

explanation.summary: The external os is the opening of the cervical canal into the vagina; the internal os opens into the uterus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cervical canal is a narrow passage connecting the uterine cavity to the vagina. Its internal os opens into the uterus, and its external os opens into the vagina, so the vaginally visible opening is the external os.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The internal os is at the uterine end of the cervical canal and cannot be seen from the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cornua are the lateral superior angles of the uterus where the uterine tubes enter the uterine cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The introitus is the vaginal opening within the vestibule of the vulva, not the cervical opening.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The interstitium is the tubal segment traversing the uterine musculature at the cornu, far from the vagina.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman delivers a healthy infant. Shortly afterward, coordinated uterine activity assists separation of the placenta from the uterine wall. The myometrial layer chiefly responsible for this function also contracts during menses to help shed the functional endometrium. Which of the following identifies this layer?

explanation.summary: The stratum subvasculare, the innermost circular myometrial layer, contracts during menses to shed the functionalis and helps separate the placenta after childbirth.
explanation.whyCorrect: The innermost layer of the myometrium, the stratum subvasculare, has a circular pattern. It contracts during menses and assists in shedding the functional layer of the endometrium, and it helps the separation of the placenta after childbirth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The stratum vasculare is the middle crisscrossing layer responsible for most uterine contraction during labor, not placental separation and menstrual shedding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stratum supravasculare is the outer longitudinal layer that stabilizes the uterine wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The stratum basalis is an endometrial layer that regenerates the functionalis; it is not myometrial muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The stratum functionalis is the shed endometrial layer itself, not a contractile muscle layer.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman conceives, and the fertilized egg travels to the uterine cavity and implants normally. Implantation occurs within which of the following layers of the uterine wall?

explanation.summary: The stratum functionalis is the site of implantation of a fertilized egg.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endometrium is divided into an upper functional layer and a lower basal layer. The stratum functionalis undergoes proliferation and shedding during the menstrual cycle, and it is also the site of implantation for a fertilized egg.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The stratum basalis is maintained through the cycle to replenish the functionalis; it is not the implantation site.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stratum vasculare is a smooth muscle layer that powers labor contractions, not a site of implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The stratum supravasculare is the outer longitudinal muscle layer that stabilizes the uterine wall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The perimetrium is the outer serosal covering of the uterus; implantation there would not be within the uterine lining.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A radiologist's report on a pelvic ultrasound describes a 'right adnexal mass' in a 35-year-old woman. The adnexa of the uterus comprise which of the following groups of structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ovaries, uterine tubes, and their supporting ligaments

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cervix, upper vagina, and the cardinal ligaments

choices.label: C
choices.text: The uterine fundus, round ligaments, and inguinal canals

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bladder, urethra, and the paraurethral glands

choices.label: E
choices.text: The rectum, anal canal, and the perineal body

explanation.summary: The adnexa of the uterus are the ovaries, the uterine tubes, and the ligaments that support them.
explanation.whyCorrect: The uterine tubes are included in the 'adnexa of the uterus,' a collective term for the structures next to the uterus: the ovaries, the uterine tubes, and the ligaments that support them. An adnexal mass therefore localizes to this lateral group of structures.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The cervix and upper vagina are midline parts of the internal reproductive tract, not the para-uterine adnexa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The fundus is part of the uterus itself, and the round ligament's course through the inguinal canal does not define the adnexa.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The bladder, urethra, and paraurethral glands belong to the urinary tract and vestibule, not the uterine adnexa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The rectum, anal canal, and perineal body are posterior perineal structures unrelated to the adnexa.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A histology instructor points out the constant beating motion of the cilia on the columnar epithelium lining the uterine tube. This ciliary motion directly accomplishes which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transporting the ovulated egg toward the uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transporting the ovulated egg toward the fimbriae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Propelling sperm from the uterus toward the ovary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circulating peritoneal fluid across the ovarian surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clearing menstrual debris into the peritoneal cavity

explanation.summary: Tubal cilia beat constantly toward the uterus, transporting the ovulated egg from the ovary toward the uterine cavity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines the lumen of the uterine tubes, and the cilia have a constant beating motion toward the uterus. They are important for transporting an ovulated egg from the ovaries toward the uterus; one of the challenges for sperm is swimming upstream against this ciliary beating.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The beat is directed toward the uterus, not back toward the fimbriated end of the tube.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sperm must swim against the ciliary current; the cilia do not propel sperm toward the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sweeping over the ovary is the role of the fimbriae capturing the oocyte, not of intraluminal ciliary flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The cilia move contents toward the uterus, the opposite direction from the peritoneal cavity.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has been unable to conceive for 2 years. Imaging shows scarred, blunted fimbriae at the distal ends of both uterine tubes, with patent tubal lumens. Which of the following best explains her infertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure to retrieve the ovulated ovum from the peritoneal space

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cessation of follicle maturation within the ovarian cortex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the endometrium to regenerate after menstruation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of mucus secretion by the endocervical glands

choices.label: E
choices.text: Absence of estrogen conversion by the granulosa cells

explanation.summary: Damage to the fimbriae from PID prevents retrieval of the ovulated ovum from the peritoneal space, causing infertility even with patent tubes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ovaries are not directly attached to the uterine tubes; the ovulated egg must be swept into the tube by the fimbriae. Conditions that inflame the tubes and damage the fimbriae, such as pelvic inflammatory disease and localized endometriosis lesions, can prevent the retrieval of the ovulated ovum from the peritoneal space or occlude the tube, preventing fertilization. Here the lumens are patent, so failed oocyte pickup is the mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.B: PID damages the tubes and fimbriae; it does not stop follicular maturation in the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrial regeneration is the role of the stratum basalis and is not affected by fimbrial scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endocervical mucus production is a cervical function unrelated to distal tubal damage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen conversion by granulosa cells is an ovarian follicular function, not a consequence of fimbrial injury.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A neuroanatomy course reviews the autonomic supply of the female pelvis. Most pelvic organs receive parasympathetic fibers from S2-S4 via the inferior hypogastric plexus, but the ovary is an exception. The ovary receives its parasympathetic innervation from which of the following sources?

explanation.summary: Unlike most pelvic organs, the ovary receives parasympathetic input from the vagus nerve and sympathetic innervation from the ovarian plexus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sympathetic fibers from T10-L2 and parasympathetic fibers from S2-S4 contribute to the inferior hypogastric (pelvic) plexus, which supplies most pelvic organs. The exception is the ovaries, which receive parasympathetic input from the vagus nerve (CN X) and sympathetic innervation by the ovarian plexus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: S2-S4 parasympathetics supply most pelvic organs through the inferior hypogastric plexus, but the ovary is the stated exception.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The pudendal nerve provides sensory innervation to the inferior vagina and external genitalia and motor innervation to the pelvic floor; it is not the ovary's parasympathetic source.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T10-L2 fibers are sympathetic, not parasympathetic, and they feed the inferior hypogastric plexus for other pelvic organs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The ovarian plexus carries the ovary's sympathetic innervation, not its parasympathetic supply.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with regular cycles is at mid-cycle when an egg is released from her ovary into the uterine tube. The egg is released from a follicle at which of the following stages of maturation?

explanation.summary: Ovulation occurs at the ovulatory (Graafian) follicle stage, the final step of the maturation sequence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each month during the reproductive years, a follicle matures under hormonal influence through the sequence primordial, primary, secondary, tertiary, and finally ovulatory (Graafian) follicle. The Graafian follicle is the stage at which ovulation occurs, when the egg is released out of the follicle and the ovary into the Fallopian tube.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Primordial follicles are the smallest follicles waiting to be activated; they make up the vast majority of follicles and do not ovulate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The primary follicle is an early maturation stage, well before ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The secondary follicle is an intermediate stage that must still progress further before ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The tertiary follicle precedes the ovulatory stage; the egg is not yet released at this point.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman does not conceive during her current cycle. Late in the cycle, the granulosa- and theca-derived structure that had been secreting estrogen and progesterone degenerates into a collagen-filled region. A fall in which of the following hormones primarily drives this change?

explanation.summary: A drop in hormones, particularly LH, converts the corpus luteum into the collagen-filled corpus albicans.
explanation.whyCorrect: After ovulation, granulosa and thecal cells left in the ovary re-organize into the corpus luteum, which secretes estrogen and progesterone to maintain the thick endometrial lining. The drop in hormones, particularly LH, causes the corpus luteum to turn into a collagen-filled region called the corpus albicans.

whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH drives follicular maturation; its fall is not what the lecture identifies as the trigger for luteal regression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen is one of the corpus luteum's own products, not the hormone whose withdrawal causes its degeneration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone is likewise secreted by the corpus luteum itself; its decline is a consequence, not the cause, of luteal regression.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolactin is not described as maintaining the corpus luteum.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman is found to have an ovarian tumor diagnosed as a thecoma. The normal counterpart of the cells composing this tumor performs which of the following functions in a developing follicle?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Covering the surface of the ovary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Filling the corpus albicans with collagen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sweeping the ovulated oocyte into the tube

explanation.summary: Thecomas arise from thecal cells; endocrine cells of the theca interna secrete progesterone and estrogen precursors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thecal cells are mesenchymal cells around the follicle, and the endocrine cells of the theca interna secrete both progesterone and estrogen precursors, which granulosa cells then convert to estrogen. Ovarian tumors can originate from both support cell types: granulosa cell tumors from granulosa cells and thecomas from thecal cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Converting the precursors into estrogen is the job of granulosa cells, whose tumor counterpart is the granulosa cell tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ovarian surface is covered by simple cuboidal mesothelium, not thecal cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus albicans is a collagen-filled remnant of the regressed corpus luteum; producing it is not the defining role of thecal cells in a developing follicle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sweeping the oocyte into the tube is the function of the fimbriae of the infundibulum.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: During laparoscopic pelvic surgery, the surgeon identifies a ligament arising from the fundus of the uterus and follows it laterally and anteriorly until it enters the inguinal canal. This ligament terminates in which of the following structures?

explanation.summary: The round ligament of the uterus runs from the uterine fundus through the inguinal canal to the labia majora.
explanation.whyCorrect: The round ligament of the uterus connects the fundus of the uterus to the labia majora, passing through the inguinal canal. A ligament traced from the fundus into the inguinal canal is therefore the round ligament, ending in the labia majora.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The labia minora are the smaller inner folds; the round ligament terminates in the labia majora.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ovary is connected to the uterus by the ovarian ligament, which does not traverse the inguinal canal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The sacrum is the attachment of the uterosacral ligament, which runs posteriorly from the cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lateral pelvic wall anchors the cardinal ligament and the suspensory ligament of the ovary, not the round ligament's termination.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for symptomatic fibroids. To mobilize the cervix and upper vagina, the surgeon must divide the ligament anchoring them to the lateral pelvic wall. Careful hemostasis is required because this ligament contains which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gonadal (ovarian) arteries from the aorta

explanation.summary: The cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament anchors the cervix and upper vagina to the lateral pelvic wall and contains the uterine vessels.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cardinal ligament, also called the transverse cervical ligament, anchors the cervix and upper vagina to the lateral pelvic wall and contains the uterine vessels. Dividing it during hysterectomy therefore requires control of the uterine vessels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The ovarian vessels and lymphatics run in the suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament of the ovary, not the cardinal ligament.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The pudendal nerve supplies the inferior vagina, external genitalia, and pelvic floor; it is not carried in the cardinal ligament.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The gonadal arteries descend from the abdominal aorta to the ovaries within the suspensory ligament, not to the cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The external iliac vein courses along the pelvic brim and is not contained within the cardinal ligament.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: During a total hysterectomy, the surgeon prepares to clamp and ligate the uterine artery near the cervix. The teaching phrase 'water under the bridge' is invoked to remind the team to identify which structure passing immediately inferior to this artery before ligation?

explanation.summary: The ureter passes inferior to the uterine artery ('water under the bridge'), putting it at risk during hysterectomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mnemonic 'water under the bridge' describes the ureter passing inferior to the uterine artery. This relationship is important during hysterectomy: the ureter must be identified before the uterine artery is ligated to avoid accidental ureteral injury.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The uterine vein drains the uterus into the internal iliac vein; it is not the 'water' of the mnemonic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The round ligament runs from the fundus through the inguinal canal to the labia majora, away from the uterine artery pedicle at the cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ovarian veins ascend with the ovarian vessels to the IVC or left renal vein and are not crossed by the uterine artery here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The uterosacral ligament runs from the cervix to the sacrum and is not the structure the mnemonic protects.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A pelvic floor physical therapist explains that the muscle responsible for voluntary closure of the urethra lies in the middle layer of the pelvic floor, at the perineal membrane in the deep perineal pouch. Which of the following muscle pairs makes up this layer?

choices.label: B
choices.text: External urethral sphincter and deep transverse perineal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superficial transverse perineal and external anal sphincter

explanation.summary: The middle pelvic floor layer, at the perineal membrane and deep perineal pouch, consists of the external urethral sphincter and the deep transverse perineal muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pelvic floor muscles form three layers from superficial to deep. The middle layer, at the perineal membrane and deep perineal pouch, contains the external urethral sphincter and the deep transverse perineal muscle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus belong to the superficial layer of the urogenital triangle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Levator ani and coccygeus form the deep layer, the pelvic diaphragm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obturator internus and piriformis are primarily hip muscles that act as the 'walls' of the pelvic bowl, supporting organs indirectly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The superficial transverse perineal and external anal sphincter are muscles of the superficial layer.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman reports chronic pelvic pain, urinary urgency, and discomfort. Examination reveals overly tight, tender pelvic floor muscles without organ descent. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Therapy that intentionally lengthens and releases the pelvic floor muscles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exercises aimed at strengthening the pelvic floor muscles

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placement of a vaginal pessary for mechanical support

choices.label: D
choices.text: A progressive program of heavy resistance lifting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sustained voluntary contraction holds of the levator ani

explanation.summary: Pelvic floor hypertonicity is treated with relaxation therapy that lengthens and releases the muscles, in contrast to the strengthening used for prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: In contrast to pelvic organ prolapse, pelvic floor hypertonicity results from overly tight pelvic floor muscles and may cause chronic pelvic pain, urinary urgency, and discomfort. Treatment often includes pelvic floor relaxation that intentionally lengthens and releases these muscles.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Strengthening is the physical therapy focus for pelvic organ prolapse, where support is inadequate; it would not release already overtight muscles.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vaginal pessaries are a first-line treatment for prolapse, not for hypertonic pelvic floor muscles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heavy lifting is listed as a risk factor for prolapse and is not a treatment for pelvic floor dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sustained contractions are a form of strengthening and would worsen, not relieve, muscle overactivity.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with postpartum hemorrhage undergoes pelvic angiography, and the catheter is advanced into the artery that supplies most of the uterus. This artery arises from which of the following vessels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior branch of the internal iliac artery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Posterior branch of the internal iliac artery

explanation.summary: The uterine artery, which supplies most of the uterus, comes from the anterior branch of the internal iliac artery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The anterior branch of the internal iliac artery supplies most of the female reproductive organs, and the uterine artery supplies most of the uterus. The lower uterine segment additionally has a dual blood supply that includes branches of the vaginal artery.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The posterior branch of the internal iliac is not described as the source of the reproductive organ supply.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The external iliac artery continues toward the lower limb and does not give off the uterine artery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The common iliac artery divides into internal and external iliacs; the uterine artery is not its direct branch.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Direct aortic origin describes the gonadal (ovarian) arteries, which are the exception supplying the ovaries.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman in her third trimester develops swelling of the left lower extremity attributed to compression of a pelvic vein by the gravid uterus. Which of the following anatomic features best explains why the left side is preferentially affected at the level of the common iliac vein?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The left common iliac vein takes a longer, oblique course crossing toward the right

choices.label: B
choices.text: The left common iliac vein must ascend to drain into the left renal vein

choices.label: C
choices.text: The left common iliac vein receives the ovarian vein directly at this level

choices.label: D
choices.text: The left common iliac vein passes through the inguinal canal with the round ligament

choices.label: E
choices.text: The left common iliac vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava at a right angle

explanation.summary: Because the left common iliac vein must cross toward the right to reach the IVC, its longer, more oblique course makes it particularly susceptible to compression.
explanation.whyCorrect: The internal and external iliac veins join to form the common iliac vein on each side, and the right and left common iliac veins unite to form the IVC. Because the left common iliac vein must cross toward the right to reach the IVC, it has a longer, more oblique course and is particularly susceptible to compression.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Drainage into the left renal vein describes the left ovarian vein, not the left common iliac vein.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ovarian veins drain to the IVC (right) or left renal vein (left); they do not empty into the common iliac vein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: It is the round ligament of the uterus that traverses the inguinal canal; the common iliac vein remains in the pelvis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The left common iliac vein does not enter the IVC by a short direct route; that is closer to the right side's arrangement.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Female Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with a dull ache in the left side of his scrotum. On examination, there is a soft, compressible mass superior to the left testis with a 'bag of worms' texture. Which of the following anatomic features best explains why this condition occurs more often on the left side?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The left gonadal artery arises from the internal iliac artery

choices.label: B
choices.text: The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein at a right angle

choices.label: C
choices.text: The left pampiniform plexus drains directly into the inferior vena cava

choices.label: D
choices.text: The left testis drains lymph to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The left spermatic cord lacks an internal spermatic fascia layer

explanation.summary: Varicocele is more common on the left because the left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein rather than directly into the inferior vena cava.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both testes drain first into the pampiniform plexus along the spermatic cord. The right gonadal vein empties directly into the inferior vena cava, but the left gonadal vein first enters the left renal vein at a right angle. This produces higher venous pressure on the left, predisposing to abnormal dilation of the pampiniform plexus (varicocele), which feels like a 'bag of worms' superior to the testis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gonadal arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta, not the internal iliac artery, and arterial anatomy does not explain venous congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: It is the right pampiniform plexus, via the right gonadal vein, that drains directly into the inferior vena cava; the left does not.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The testes drain lymph to the para-aortic nodes, not the superficial inguinal nodes, and lymphatic drainage does not cause varicocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The spermatic cord on both sides is wrapped in external spermatic fascia, cremasteric muscle, and internal spermatic fascia; no layer is missing on the left.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with biopsy-proven prostate cancer develops progressive low back pain. Imaging shows multiple metastatic lesions in the lumbar vertebral bodies. Which of the following routes best explains this pattern of spread?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lymphatic spread through the para-aortic lymph nodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct extension of tumor through the posterior rectal wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arterial seeding via branches of the inferior vesical artery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Venous connection between the prostatic and vertebral plexuses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lymphatic spread through the superficial inguinal lymph nodes

explanation.summary: Prostatic venous drainage communicates with the vertebral venous plexus, making vertebrae the most common site of prostate cancer metastasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The prostate drains first into the prostatic plexus and then into the internal iliac vein, which is connected to the vertebral venous plexus. This venous connection provides a direct route for tumor cells to reach the vertebrae, which is why vertebrae are the most common sites for prostate cancer metastasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Para-aortic nodes are the first metastatic site for testicular cancer, which drains along the gonadal vessels, not the typical route for prostatic spread to bone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The rectum lies posterior to the prostate, but the vertebral metastases described are explained by venous spread, not direct extension through the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The inferior vesical artery supplies blood to the prostate; arterial inflow is not the described route of metastatic outflow to the vertebrae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Superficial inguinal nodes drain the scrotum; the prostate drains primarily to internal iliac and sacral nodes, and the vertebral spread here is venous.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man reports a weak urinary stream, hesitancy, and waking three times nightly to urinate. Digital rectal examination shows a smoothly enlarged, nontender prostate. Enlargement of which of the following regions of the prostate is most likely responsible for his urinary symptoms?

explanation.summary: The transitional zone, though only about 5% of prostate volume, causes most symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia by compressing the prostatic urethra.
explanation.whyCorrect: The transitional zone makes up only about 5% of prostate volume but is responsible for most symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia. Because it immediately surrounds the prostatic urethra, its enlargement compresses the urethral lumen and produces obstructive urinary symptoms such as weak stream and nocturia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The peripheral zone comprises up to 70% of prostate volume and is the most common site of prostate cancer, but it is not the zone that produces BPH symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The central zone comprises roughly 25% of the gland and surrounds the ejaculatory ducts; it is not the region implicated in BPH symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The anterior fibromuscular stroma is a thickened band of tissue surrounding the prostatic apex, not a glandular zone that hypertrophies to obstruct the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The membranous urethra lies distal to the prostate; it is not a region of the prostate and is not enlarged in BPH.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is evaluated for infertility. He reports that very little fluid is expelled when he climaxes, and a urine sample collected immediately afterward contains abundant sperm. Which of the following abnormalities best explains these findings?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Weakness of the sphincter at the base of the bladder

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absent secretory function of the seminal vesicles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of peristalsis in the vas deferens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prior ligation of both vas deferens

explanation.summary: Weakness of the sphincter at the base of the bladder causes retrograde ejaculation, in which semen passes backward into the bladder and can cause infertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: A sphincter at the base of the bladder normally prevents urination during ejaculation and keeps semen moving outward. When this sphincter is weak, sperm travel backward into the bladder rather than outward (retrograde ejaculation), producing a low-volume ejaculate, sperm in the post-climax urine, and infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Obstructed ejaculatory ducts could reduce ejaculate volume, but they would not deliver abundant sperm into the bladder and urine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of seminal vesicle secretions would lower ejaculate volume, since they contribute 70-85% of it, but it would not place sperm in the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sympathetically driven peristalsis of the vas deferens propels sperm forward; its failure would not push sperm backward into the bladder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasectomy prevents sperm from reaching the ejaculate at all, so sperm would be absent from both the ejaculate and the urine.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man is found to have a firm, painless mass in his right testis. Biopsy confirms testicular cancer. A CT scan is ordered to evaluate for nodal metastasis. Which group of lymph nodes is the most likely site of initial spread?

explanation.summary: The testes drain lymph along the gonadal vessels to the para-aortic (lateral aortic) nodes, the first site of testicular cancer metastasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testicular lymphatic vessels run alongside the gonadal arteries to the para-aortic (lateral aortic) retroperitoneal nodes, which lie anterior to the lumbar vertebrae near the abdominal aorta. These nodes are the most common site for initial metastasis of testicular cancers, which is why CT imaging is used to assess nodal involvement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Superficial inguinal nodes drain the scrotum, not the testis itself.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Deep inguinal nodes, together with superficial inguinal nodes, drain the penis rather than the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Internal iliac nodes are a primary drainage site for the prostate, not the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sacral nodes drain the prostate along with the internal iliac nodes; they are not the first stop for testicular lymph.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a chronic ulcerated lesion confined to the skin of the scrotum. Biopsy shows carcinoma. Which group of lymph nodes should be examined first for regional metastasis?

explanation.summary: Although the scrotum lies next to the testes, its lymph drains to the superficial inguinal nodes, not the para-aortic nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The scrotum, despite its proximity to the testes, drains to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes. This contrasts sharply with the testes themselves, which drain along the gonadal vessels to the para-aortic nodes. A carcinoma limited to scrotal skin therefore spreads first to the superficial inguinal group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Para-aortic nodes receive lymph from the testes, not from the overlying scrotal skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Deep inguinal nodes participate in draining the penis; the scrotum drains to the superficial inguinal group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Internal iliac nodes are primary drainage for the prostate, not the scrotum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sacral nodes drain the prostate together with internal iliac nodes and do not receive scrotal lymph.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man considering a vasectomy worries that he will no longer ejaculate any fluid afterward. His physician reassures him that ejaculate volume changes very little. Which of the following structures contributes the largest share of seminal fluid volume?

explanation.summary: The seminal vesicles produce roughly 70-85% of total seminal fluid volume, which is unaffected by vasectomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The seminal vesicles secrete a fructose-rich fluid containing proteins, enzymes, and nutrients that makes up roughly 70-85% of total seminal fluid volume. Because vasectomy severs only the vas deferens, the seminal vesicles and prostate continue to contribute their secretions, so ejaculate volume changes little; it simply lacks sperm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The testes produce sperm and testosterone; sperm contribute only a small fraction of ejaculate volume.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The epididymis stores and matures sperm; it is not a major fluid-producing gland.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The bulbourethral glands secrete a clear lubricating pre-ejaculate that does not contribute to final seminal fluid volume.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vas deferens is a muscular transport tube for sperm, not a secretory source of seminal fluid.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A histology slide shows a tubular structure lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia. Its thick muscular wall contains a central layer of smooth muscle fibers encircling the lumen, sandwiched between two longitudinal layers. Which of the following structures is shown?

explanation.summary: The vas deferens is identified by stereociliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium plus a three-layered smooth muscle wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vas deferens is lined with stereociliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium and has three smooth muscle layers in its wall: a central layer with fibers circling the lumen and two surrounding longitudinal layers. These layers contract reflexively and forcefully during ejaculation to propel sperm forward.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The epididymis also has pseudostratified epithelium with stereocilia, but it is described as a two-layered epithelium-lined storage tube, not a duct with a prominent three-layered muscular wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The seminal vesicle is a tubular gland of pseudostratified columnar cells that secretes fructose-rich fluid; it is not defined by three organized smooth muscle layers around a transport lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The bulbourethral gland is a tubuloalveolar gland composed of lobules of acini, not a muscular transport duct.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The prostate consists of convoluted two-layered glands within a fibromuscular stroma, not a single stereociliated tube with layered muscle.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man presents with several days of scrotal pain. Examination shows tenderness and swelling localized to a convoluted structure posterior to the left testis. He is diagnosed with a bacterial infection of this structure and started on antibiotics. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause in this patient?

explanation.summary: Epididymitis in older males is most commonly caused by Escherichia coli, whereas gonococcus predominates in young males.
explanation.whyCorrect: The structure described is the epididymis, the long convoluted tube posterior to the testis responsible for sperm storage and maturation. Epididymitis is commonly caused by gonococcus in young males but by Escherichia coli in older males, and it responds well to antibiotics. In a 67-year-old, E. coli is the most likely organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonococcal epididymitis is typical of young males, not a 67-year-old.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus aureus is not the organism associated with epididymitis in older males.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is not the typical cause of epididymitis in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes is not the organism linked to epididymitis in older males.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man undergoes prostate biopsy for a suspicious nodule. Throughout the abnormal areas, the glands are lined by only a single layer of epithelial cells, with no identifiable second cell layer at the gland periphery. Which of the following best explains the significance of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is normal, because prostatic glands are lined by one cell layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: It indicates benign hyperplasia of the transitional zone

choices.label: C
choices.text: It indicates adenocarcinoma, with loss of the basal cell layer

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reflects age-related deposition of corpora amylacea

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reflects lipofuscin accumulation within secretory cells

explanation.summary: Normal prostatic glands have a two-layered epithelium; loss of the deep basal layer, leaving a single layer, marks prostatic adenocarcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normal prostatic glands are lined by a two-layered epithelium: an inner row of pale columnar secretory cells with large basal nuclei and a deeper row of squamous regenerative cells with flat nuclei. In prostatic cancer the epithelium has only one layer, so progressive loss of the basal epithelial layer across the glands indicates adenocarcinoma rather than normal tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Normal prostatic epithelium is two-layered; a single layer is the abnormality that distinguishes cancer, even though the deep layer can be difficult to see.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Benign prostatic hyperplasia arises from the transitional zone and causes urethral compression; it is not defined by loss of the basal cell layer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Corpora amylacea are glycoprotein and keratan sulfate concretions in gland lumens that increase with age and have no clinical significance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lipofuscin granules are yellow pigments from dead epithelial cells described in the seminal vesicles, tinting seminal fluid; they do not explain a missing cell layer.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man undergoes radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. After surgery, he is unable to achieve an erection. Injury to which of the following nerves during the operation best explains this complication?

explanation.summary: The pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4), which run near the prostate and drive erection, are at risk during prostatectomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasympathetic innervation of the pelvic organs arises from S2-S4 as the pelvic splanchnic nerves, which travel on the walls of the rectum close to the prostate. These parasympathetic fibers dilate penile blood vessels to produce erection (the 'point' phase). Their proximity to the prostate puts them at risk of injury during prostatectomy, causing erectile dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The pudendal nerve (S2-S4) provides somatic motor and sensory innervation to pelvic and perineal structures, not the parasympathetic vasodilation that produces erection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The hypogastric nerve (L1-L2) carries sympathetic fibers, which constrict penile vessels and drive ejaculation rather than erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The vagus nerve supplies parasympathetic innervation to the testes, not to the penile vessels, and does not course near the prostate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The obturator nerve is not described as supplying autonomic input to the penile vasculature.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: The penis contains three cylindrical masses of erectile tissue. Which of the following structures surrounds and protects the spongy (penile) urethra?

explanation.summary: The single ventral corpus spongiosum surrounds and protects the spongy (penile) urethra.
explanation.whyCorrect: The penis is composed of two paired corpora cavernosa dorsally and a single corpus spongiosum ventrally. The corpus spongiosum surrounds and protects the spongy (penile) urethra, the shared final passage for semen and urine during ejaculation and urination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The corpora cavernosa are the paired dorsal erectile bodies; they do not contain the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The prepuce (foreskin) covers the glans externally and does not enclose the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The frenulum attaches the prepuce ventrally to the glans; it is not erectile tissue around the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The prostatic fibromuscular stroma surrounds prostatic glands around the prostatic urethra, not the spongy urethra in the penis.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with a small, painful tear of a band of tissue on the ventral surface of the glans penis that he sustained during intercourse. The injured band normally attaches the foreskin to the glans. Which of the following structures was injured?

explanation.summary: The frenulum is the ventral band of tissue that attaches the prepuce (foreskin) to the glans penis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The body of the penis ends in the glans, which is covered by the prepuce (foreskin). The prepuce is attached to the glans ventrally by the frenulum, so a tear of the ventral tissue band connecting foreskin to glans is a frenulum injury.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The prepuce is the foreskin itself, the fold of skin covering the glans; it is anchored by the frenulum rather than being the attaching band.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The corpus spongiosum is the single ventral cylinder of erectile tissue surrounding the spongy urethra, not a skin attachment on the glans.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpora cavernosa are the paired dorsal erectile bodies of the penis and do not attach the foreskin to the glans.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The bulbospongiosus is a superficial pelvic floor muscle overlying the bulb of the penis, not a band of tissue on the glans.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A histopathologist traces the route that newly produced sperm follow as they leave the testis. After passing through the straight seminiferous tubules, the sperm next enter which of the following structures?

explanation.summary: Sperm pass from the straight seminiferous tubules into the rete testis before being transported to the epididymis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once sperm are produced in the testes, they pass through the rete testis, which lies distal to the straight seminiferous tubules. Only after the rete testis are they transported distally to the epididymis. The SEVEN UP memory aid intentionally omits the rete testis and efferent ductules, which are part of the complete anatomical pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The epididymis receives sperm after they have passed through the rete testis, not directly from the seminiferous tubules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The vas deferens carries sperm onward from the epididymis, several steps later in the pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ejaculatory ducts form where the vas deferens joins the seminal vesicle ducts, far downstream of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The seminal vesicles are secretory glands that contribute fluid to semen; sperm are not produced in or routed through them from the testis.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: During a pelvic dissection, a student identifies the paired ejaculatory ducts as they enter the prostate. The ejaculatory ducts are formed by the union of which of the following pairs of structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vas deferens and excretory duct of the seminal vesicle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vas deferens and duct of the bulbourethral gland

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excretory duct of the seminal vesicle and prostatic urethra

explanation.summary: Each ejaculatory duct forms where the vas deferens merges with the excretory duct of the seminal vesicle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Seminal fluid exits the seminal vesicles via excretory ducts, which merge with the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory ducts. These ducts then empty into the urethra within the prostate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The epididymis is continuous with the vas deferens proximally; their junction does not create the ejaculatory duct.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The bulbourethral glands lie distal to the prostatic urethra and secrete lubricating pre-ejaculate; they do not join the vas deferens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rete testis and epididymis are connected early in the sperm pathway, within and just beyond the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The ejaculatory ducts empty into the prostatic urethra, but the urethra is their destination, not one of the two structures whose union forms them.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: During ejaculation, sperm-containing seminal fluid and prostatic secretions come to share a single passageway. At which of the following sites do these two fluids first mix?

explanation.summary: The two ejaculatory ducts merge at the prostatic urethra, where seminal fluid first mixes with prostatic secretions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Within the prostate, the two ejaculatory ducts merge at the prostatic urethra. This is where seminal fluid and prostatic secretions mix and begin to share a passageway for ejaculation through the urethra. Distal to the prostate, the urethra continues briefly as the membranous urethra before entering the penis as the spongy urethra.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The membranous urethra lies distal to the prostate; the fluids have already mixed by the time they reach it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The spongy (penile) urethra is the final exit passage for semen, well beyond the point of first mixing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ejaculatory ducts carry the mixture of sperm and seminal vesicle fluid, but prostatic secretions are not added until the ducts empty into the prostatic urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The base of the bladder contains the sphincter that prevents urination during ejaculation; semen normally does not enter this region.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man undergoing an infertility evaluation provides a semen sample. The laboratory notes that the specimen fails to coagulate after ejaculation. Deficient secretion of which of the following substances best explains this finding?

explanation.summary: Semenogelin, a protein produced by the seminal vesicles, is responsible for semen coagulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The seminal vesicles produce the protein semenogelin, which makes semen coagulate. A specimen that fails to coagulate therefore points to a deficiency of semenogelin in the seminal vesicle secretion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fructose in seminal vesicle fluid provides energy for the sperm; it does not cause coagulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipofuscin consists of yellow pigment granules from dead epithelial cells that can tint seminal fluid; it has no coagulating role.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratan sulfate is a component of corpora amylacea, the concretions found in prostatic gland lumens, not a coagulating protein of semen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone is a sex hormone synthesized by the testes; it is not a seminal protein responsible for coagulation.

questions.topicName: Anatomy and Histology of the Male Reproductive System

questions.stem: The secretion of the seminal vesicles contains proteins, enzymes, and nutrients. A particularly high concentration of which of the following components serves as the energy source for sperm?

explanation.summary: Seminal vesicle fluid has an especially high concentration of fructose, which provides energy for sperm.
explanation.whyCorrect: The seminal vesicles produce a secretion containing various proteins, enzymes, and nutrients, with an especially high concentration of fructose. This fructose provides the energy that powers the sperm.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Semenogelin is the seminal vesicle protein that makes semen coagulate; it is not the sperm's energy substrate.
